clue.text: Essential details provided by supporters — lots

parts.note: bras are garments that support the bust
stacks means a great deal, as in stacks of money

explanation.surface: A note that the key facts come courtesy of plenty of backers.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'getting down to brass tacks' means dealing with the basic practical facts.

clue.text: Mate in America had developed godlike figure

parts.note: bud, short for buddy, is American slang for a friend

indicators.note: developed suggests something worked into a new form, so the letters of had are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American friend has grown into someone almost divine.
explanation.definitionFit: The founder of Buddhism is revered as an enlightened, near-divine teacher.

clue.text: Beer to welcome supporter, say, in accusing manner

indicators.note: to welcome means to take a guest in, so the beer word wraps round the limb

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a leg supports a body or a table

explanation.surface: A pint offered to a fan, apparently, while pointing the finger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like the usual 'for example' tag on supporter, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To claim something accusingly, usually without proof yet, is to state it as a charge.

clue.text: Disorganised spread knocked on the head

parts.note: to scatter is to spread widely
brained means hit hard on the head

explanation.surface: Someone muddled, scattered about and dazed from a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: someone hopelessly disorganised and forgetful is described as flighty or muddled-headed.

clue.text: Evaluates a page and expresses approval

parts.note: praises means speaks approvingly of

explanation.surface: A reviewer assesses a page and voices approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess the worth or quality of something is to value or judge it.

clue.text: Mineral found within the borders of Kamchatka Peninsula

indicators.note: found within says the mineral sits inside the other letters
the borders of a word are its outside letters, its first and last

parts.note: ore is mineral-bearing rock

explanation.surface: Mineral deposits discovered on the edge of Kamchatka Peninsula in Russia's far east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kamchatka Peninsula' reads as one place name; 'Peninsula' is split off as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Korean landmass is a peninsula jutting from mainland Asia.

clue.text: Measure pace

definitions.meaning: an action taken, as in taking measures

explanation.surface: Instructions to gauge a stride.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an action taken towards a goal; the other is a single stride of the feet.

clue.text: Drink most of time, welcoming a song

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the shortened word wraps round the a
most of means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: the word time itself, shortened
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: Drinking for most of the evening while a tune is welcomed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims the final E from TIME to give TIM, which takes in A.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand of coffee liqueur from Jamaica, served as an after-dinner drink.

clue.text: Standing of inebriated priest, say, on the up

indicators.note: a drunk person is all over the place, so the letters of priest are jumbled
in a down clue, on the up means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: e.g. means for example, which is what say means here

explanation.surface: A tipsy cleric's reputation, supposedly, is improving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the up' turns EG into GE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing and prestige both mean the status and esteem in which someone is held.

clue.text: Embarrassing person better learn if swaggering around North

indicators.note: around says the jumbled letters go round the compass point
swaggering suggests a loose, rolling movement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to a cocky northerner who keeps embarrassing everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North' reads as a region the swaggerer comes from, but it is just the compass letter placed inside the rearranged words.
explanation.definitionFit: French for 'terrible child', used of someone whose outrageous behaviour embarrasses their associates.

clue.text: Part of river Dee?

parts.note: the mouth of a river can fan out into this landform, and Dee is also the sound of the letter D, whose Greek counterpart has this name

explanation.surface: A geography question about a section of the River Dee in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: Dee is a British river, but also the letter D spelt out; the Greek letter for D shares its name with a river mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a fan of sediment at a river mouth and the Greek name for the letter D.

clue.text: Start to pay a lease on mature stock

indicators.note: the start to a word is its first letter

parts.note: to rent is to lease
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: Instructions to begin paying for leased livestock that has grown up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' looks like livestock or shares but means ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock in the sense of descent or lineage: someone of good stock has good ancestry.

clue.text: Meal that may be served up?

definitions.text: Meal that may be served up?

parts.words: Meal that may be served up?
parts.note: an early evening meal of tea and cooked food; read playfully, a cuppa served up high

explanation.surface: Simply asking which meal gets served.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this is a substantial early-evening meal with tea, often in the north; the clue imagines tea raised up.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooked early-evening meal eaten with tea, traditional in northern England and Scotland.

clue.text: Determined a time to employ staff after commercial

indicators.note: after places the following letters behind the advertisement

parts.note: an ad is a commercial

indicators.note: to employ means taking on, so the a and time letters take in the staff

parts.note: to man is to staff

explanation.surface: A firm set on hiring workers following an advertising campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unshakeable in their resolve is firmly set and refuses to budge.

clue.text: Encourage hurtful story that's kept out of newspaper?

definitions.text: story that's kept out of newspaper?

parts.note: to press someone is to urge them on
a cutting remark is wounding

explanation.surface: Urging on a damaging story that an editor has spiked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept out of' sounds like suppressed, but means clipped from the paper and kept.
explanation.definitionFit: An article clipped from a newspaper and saved is literally kept, once cut out.

clue.text: Register and turn left, oddly, for game

parts.note: to clock is to register or record, as in clocking a speed
a go is a turn in a game

indicators.note: oddly picks the first and third letters, the odd-numbered positions

explanation.surface: Sign in and turn left at odd moments to play.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawn game where players putt from points arranged in a circle like a clock face.

clue.text: Stayed ahead after depositing gold in Slough

indicators.note: after places the lead word behind the gold-filled one
depositing means placing something down inside
in says the gold goes inside the other word

parts.note: to slough is to shed, as a snake sheds skin
or is gold in heraldry
up means ahead, as in a team being up

explanation.surface: Someone stayed in the lead after banking gold in the Berkshire town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, but here a verb meaning shed.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay something is to prop or support it, which is what shoring does.

clue.text: Phone about second point of sale and removal

indicators.note: about means round, so the phone word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to dial is to phone
POS is the abbreviation for point of sale

explanation.surface: Ringing round about a till and getting rid of goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting rid of something is its disposal, a synonym for taking it away.

clue.text: Hear terror is spreading — some may replace locks

indicators.note: spreading means the letters scatter, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: News of panic spreading, with talk of changing the locks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' suggests doors and security; it means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic claimed to regrow hair, replacing lost tresses on a bald head.

clue.text: Perhaps butterfly's light touch

definitions.meaning: butterfly is an example of a swimming style
a gentle caress with the hand

explanation.surface: A butterfly's delicate brush against the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterfly is one swimming style; separately, a gentle movement of the hand over something.

clue.text: A new set point, darlings!

parts.note: to gel is to set firm
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A theatrical type greeting a freshly made point with luvvie enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Angels is an affectionate address for dear ones, like sweethearts.

clue.text: Copy most of response, taking heart from vicar

indicators.note: most of drops the final letter

parts.note: a reply is a response

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its letters without the ends

explanation.surface: Echoing much of a reply, drawing courage from the clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: An exact duplicate made of an original, especially of an artwork.

clue.text: A film role on its own

parts.note: an actor's part is their role

explanation.surface: An actor's solo role in a film.
explanation.definitionFit: Set aside separately from others, standing alone.

clue.text: Jack ultimately has age and can nail constituent

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter

parts.note: an era is an age
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Jack is getting on and can do a DIY job with nails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can nail' suggests hammering, but 'nail constituent' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The fibrous protein forming fingernails, hair and horn.

clue.text: A person ignoring danger varies road speed

indicators.note: varies means changes, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A reckless driver keeps changing speed on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless outlaw who takes wild risks and has no regard for safety.

clue.text: Black slime in drink

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
ooze is soft mud or slime

explanation.surface: Something dark and gooey found in a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for alcohol, any intoxicating liquor.

clue.text: European source of energy after reversing cut

indicators.note: after places the energy letter behind the turned-round word
reversing means the word for cut is read backwards

parts.note: to lop is to cut off

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A European energy supplier after a policy U-turn on cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Poland, a country of central Europe.

clue.text: Fellow twice taken in by patrolling sentries gets drinks

indicators.note: taken in by says the doubled letter goes inside
patrolling sentries walk about, so their letters move around
twice means the letter appears two times

explanation.surface: A man captured twice by guards on their rounds is given a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff drinks of spirits, taken to brace oneself, are informally called stiffeners.
